method: Let's sketch out a design that seems impossible to create in Microsoft Word, and then try to recreate someone else's work within the program; hopefully, this will help us gain a better understanding of the software and the projects involved.There is a price to pay for using any tool; our job is to figure out what that price is and whether it is worth it.

1 — The environmental cost of chargers extends beyond the disposal phase
A 2017 life-cycle assessment of mobile phone chargers found that the usage phase accounted for approximately 94.4% and 70% of the environmental impact regarding resource depletion and global warming, respectively. In contrast, for other environmental impact categories, the pre-manufacturing phase contributed over 98% of the impact. The study identified Printed Board Assembly (PBA) and casing production as significant sources of impact during the pre-manufacturing phase.
The study also compared virgin PC (polycarbonate) plastic with recycled PC plastic; results showed that the impact of recycled PC regarding resource depletion was about 30% that of virgin PC, while for certain other environmental indicators, it was less than 5% of the impact associated with virgin material.
https://www.kci.go.kr/kciportal/ci/sereArticleSearch/ciSereArtiView.kci?sereArticleSearchBean.artiId=ART002300013
https://www.jksee.or.kr/journal/view.php?doi=10.4491/KSEE.2017.39.12.698

2 — Electronic components may account for a greater share of manufacturing-related environmental impact than the casing
A study on universal mobile chargers examined over 50 different models and conducted a life-cycle comparison. It noted that a charger's weight could represent 30–40% of the combined material weight of the mobile phone and the charger itself.
More importantly, the study found that over 70% of the environmental impact during the manufacturing phase stemmed from electronic components rather than the external plastic and metal structures. It also revealed significant differences in energy efficiency among chargers—differences primarily linked to internal circuit design that could not be determined solely by rated power output. Source: Environmental Benefits of a Universal Mobile Charger and Energy-aware Survey on Current Products
https://www.researchgate.net/publication/239762230_Environmental_benefits_of_a_Universal_Mobile_Charger_and_energy-aware_survey_on_current_products

3 — PCBs are complex structures composed of various materials
Annamalai and Gurumurthy conducted a material analysis of printed circuit boards (PCBs) from discarded mobile phones. The study found that PCBs may contain base metals such as copper, zinc, iron, nickel, and lead; metals with recovery value such as gold, silver, and palladium; and potentially hazardous materials such as cadmium, lead, and mercury. Source: Annamalai, M. & Gurumurthy, K., Characterization of end-of-life mobile phone printed circuit boards
Source: Annamalai, M. & Gurumurthy, K., Characterization of end-of-life mobile phone printed circuit boards
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32841086/
https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10962247.2020.1813836

4. New Interview source
The concept of a "universal" charger addresses the issue of incompatibility among long-standing charging interfaces.
An EU study cited by Reuters revealed that among chargers sold with mobile phones in 2018, approximately 50% used USB Micro-B, 29% used USB-C, and 21% used Lightning. These figures demonstrate that, even during a period of widespread smartphone adoption, multiple distinct charging systems persisted in the market. Source: Reuters / Euronews, EU plans to legislate for common phone charger
https://www.euronews.com/2021/09/21/eu-common-charger

5 — Discarded chargers themselves constitute electronic waste.
In a 2022 report on the EU's "common charger" regulations, TechCrunch noted that, according to EU estimates, unused or discarded chargers generate approximately 11,000 tonnes of electronic waste annually.
Consequently, the new common charger rules not only mandate a unified USB-C port but also allow consumers to opt out of purchasing a new external power supply when buying certain devices.
When examining the evolution of "universal chargers," I discovered a clear contradiction. Universal chargers initially sought to reduce compatibility issues by enabling a single charging unit to work with various batteries; however, as removable phone batteries gradually faded from the mainstream market, the use cases for such devices also disappeared.
Thus, a product once intended to solve problems related to redundant purchases and compatibility can itself become electronic waste as technological systems evolve.
Source: TechCrunch, Europe seals deal on USB Type-C common charger rules
TechCrunch- https://techcrunch.com/2022/06/07/eu-common-charger-usb-c

6. News / Interview source 3 — Reducing bundled chargers cannot solve the electronic waste problem on its own.
WIRED interviewed experts on electronic waste when discussing the decision to stop bundling power adapters with the iPhone 12. The article noted that the world generated approximately 53.6 million tonnes of electronic waste in 2019, a figure projected to rise to around 74 million tonnes by 2030.
The report also pointed out that removing chargers from product packaging addresses only a small fraction of the overall electronic waste issue. If consumers are forced to purchase separate adapters due to port incompatibility, this may create additional demand for packaging and shipping. Source: WIRED, The iPhone 12 Ships Without a Charger. Will It Curb E-Waste?
https://www.wired.com/story/apple-iphone-no-charger-gallium-nitride

7. Government/Parliamentary source — Repairability and product lifespan are becoming part of e-waste policy.
Research from the UK House of Commons Library on "Right to Repair" regulations notes that the Ecodesign regulations introduced in the UK in 2021 aim to improve the resource efficiency of certain electrical appliances. These measures include reducing energy consumption and electrical waste, as well as requiring manufacturers to provide spare parts and technical repair information to professional repairers.
As these regulations do not specifically target "universal chargers," I am not citing them as direct mandates that such a product must follow; rather, I am using them to provide policy context regarding the lifecycle and repairability of electronic products.
Source: House of Commons Library, Right to Repair Regulations
https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-9302

8. Commercial/trade publication — The "universal charger" has long been promoted as both a convenience and an environmental solution.
In 2009, the industry publication *Electronic Design* reported on the GSMA Universal Charging Solution, noting industry projections that a standardized charging scheme could reduce standby energy consumption by approximately 50% and prevent the production of up to 51,000 tonnes of redundant chargers.
Companies participating in the initiative included major mobile phone and telecommunications firms such as Nokia, Samsung, Sony Ericsson, Motorola, and Vodafone.
It should be noted that these figures represent industry forecasts of the scheme's potential impact, rather than actual environmental outcomes achieved. Source: Electronic Design, Universal AC Wall Adapters Will Support Future GSM Cell Phones
https://www.electronicdesign.com/technologies/power/power-supply/power-electronics-systems/article/21191383/universal-ac-wall-adapters-will-support-future-gsm-cell-phones

9. Mintel report — Longer mobile phone usage cycles are changing the significance of chargers
Mintel’s *UK Smartphones Market Report 2026* notes that SIM-only contracts account for 48% of the UK smartphone market, while nearly one-third of consumers use their phones for more than three years.
Mintel attributes this shift to factors such as cost-of-living pressures, the diminishing appeal of hardware upgrades, and extended device lifespans.
How long can a charger remain useful while the devices around it continue to change?
Source: Mintel, UK Smartphones Market Report 2026
https://store.mintel.com/report/uk-smartphones-market-report

We also discussed the definition of art in linguistic terms, citing numerous examples that remain relevant to contemporary art.
Regarding email: while its invention was intended to save time, people often spend so much time sending and replying to messages that, in reality, little time is actually saved.
The "URL War": search engines automatically curate and recommend content for you, but how do you distinguish what is truly important to you from what is not? AI has effectively superseded most websites.HTML, CSS, and JS offer a unique experience of the digital world; it is a constructed realm where everything is computed, highlighting the immense power of the web as a medium.
title: The second week of getting things on the right track
introduction: This lesson focuses on concepts: software and networks are designed to solve specific problems; while they assist you, they also "prescribe" how you work. Artists should not merely be consumers but should ask, "What do we lose by using this tool?" The lesson also explains and expands upon certain technical terms.
